title: Kheseen Biota, Mongolia
summary: Phosphorite beds of the Khesen (Kheseen) Formation in northern Mongolia preserve three-dimensional microfossils of the Doushantuo type, including embryo-like Megasphaera. Their age is disputed: a 2017 study placed them in the latest Ediacaran, while later work dates them to about 534-531 Ma, in the earliest Cambrian.

uncertainty.note: The 2017 study gives only 'latest Ediacaran' (no number in the opened abstract); the later basin study gives 534-531 Ma. The 550 Ma start is the id's nominal age, not a measured date.

where.modern_name: Khuvsgul (Khovsgol) basin, northern Mongolia (pin at Lake Khuvsgul; exact outcrop not given in opened pages)
where.historical_name: No polity; Khuvsgul terrane, an arc-related basin

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: PALEOMAP gives 9.66 S, 1.60 E for the same point at 535 Ma; MULLER2019 does not cover this age. The models disagree widely and the Khuvsgul terrane was a separate arc fragment, so treat the position as indicative only.

importance.justification: A phosphatized microfossil assemblage whose Ediacaran versus Cambrian age bears on how late Ediacaran-type forms persisted.
